THE HON'BLE SRI JUSTICE MUMMINENI SUDHEER KUMAR  WRIT PETITION No.13045 of 2023 ORDER:
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri B.Prasanna Kumar, learned Standing Counsel for the respondent.

2. This Writ Petition is filed seeking to declare the action of the respondent in not re-issuing the petitioner's passport bearing No.K4734851 vide proceedings No.HY1075103766123, dated 31.03.2023, as arbitrary and illegal.

3. A perusal of the record would reveal that the petitioner herein is involved in a criminal case vide Crime No.07 of 2022 of Women Police Station, Karimnagar District, registered for the offence under Section 498A of I.P.C. and Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.

After completion of investigation, the police filed charge sheet and the same was taken on file vide C.C.No.28 of 2023 pending on the file of Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Special Mobile (Excise) Court, Karimnagar.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Special Mobile (Excise) Court, Karimnagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 4. The petitioner herein is holder of passport bearing No.K4734851 and the same was expired on 07.08.2022.
She is a housewife.
She had submitted an application for re-issue of MSK,J wp_13045_2023 the said passport vide application No. 22-1015129877, dated 23.02.2023 by paying requisite fee.
The respondent herein is not re-issuing her passport on the ground of pendency of the aforesaid criminal case.
5. The petitioner herein is arraigned as accused No.3 in the aforesaid crime.
Now, she contends that she was falsely implicated in the aforesaid crime.
Further, she is also ready to co-operative with the trial.
Therefore, she sought to issue necessary directions to the respondent for consideration of her application to re-issue her passport.

6. It is also relevant to note that the Hon'ble Apex Court in Vangala Kasturi Rangacharuyulu v.
Central Bureau of Investigation1 had an occasion to examine the provisions of the Passports Act,
pendency of criminal cases and held that refusal of a passport can be only in case where an applicant is convicted during the period of five (5) years immediately preceding the date of application for an offence involving moral turpitude and sentence for imprisonment for not less than two years.

sentences.text: Section 6.2 (f) relates to a situation where the applicant is facing trial in a criminal Court.

The petitioner therein was convicted in a case for the offences under Sections 420, 468, 471 2020 Crl.L.J (SC) 572 MSK,J wp_13045_2023 and 477A read with 120B of the IPC and also Section 13 (2)
read with Section 13 (1) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.
Against which, an appeal was filed and the same was dismissed.
The sentence was reduced to a period of one (01) year.
The petitioner therein had approached the Hon'ble Apex Court by way of filing an appeal and the same is pending.

Therefore, considering the said facts, the Hon'ble Apex Court held that Passport Authority Khairunnissa Begum vs The Regional Pass Port Office on 5 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79037181/
1 cannot refuse renewal of the passport on the ground of pendency of the criminal appeal.

sentences.text:
Thus, the Hon'ble Apex Court directed the Passport Authority to renew the passport of the applicant without raising the objection relating to the pendency of the aforesaid criminal appeal in S.C.
7.
As discussed above, there is criminal case pending against the petitioner herein.
The aforesaid passport of the petitioner was expired on 07.08.2022.
She had submitted an application on 23.02.2023 for re-issue of her passport.
The respondent is not considering the application for re-issue on the ground of pendency of the aforesaid criminal case.
On the ground of pendency of the proceedings in criminal cases, the respondents cannot deny re-issue of passport of the petitioner herein.
There is no provision in the Passports Act or Rules/Regulations that passport cannot be granted on the MSK,J wp_13045_2023 ground of pendency of criminal cases.
Further, the petitioner herein is standing on better footing than the petitioner in Vangala Kasturi Rangacharyulu's case (1 supra).
In view of the same, the respondent cannot deny or refuse to renew the passport of the petitioner.
However, if the petitioner is intending to travel abroad, she has to approach trial Court in the aforesaid criminal case and obtain permission for travelling abroad.

In the present writ petition, the petitioner is not seeking permission to travel abroad, and she is seeking only re-issuance of her passport.
8.

(iii) The petitioner herein shall submit an application afresh along with certified copy of this order as well as the aforesaid undertaking MSK,J wp_13045_2023 before the Passport Officer/Authority concerned for renewal of her passport.

(iv) On filing such an application, the Passport Officer/Authority shall consider the same afresh in the light of the observations made by this Court herein as well as the contents of the undertaking given by the petitioner for re-issue of her passport in accordance with law, within three (3) weeks from the date of said application.

(v) On renewal of the passport, the petitioner herein shall deposit the original renewed passport before the trial Court in C.C.No.28 of 2023; and Khairunnissa Begum vs The Regional Pass Port Office on 5 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79037181/

In view of the aforesaid discussion, this Writ Petition is disposed of directing the respondent herein to consider the application No.22-1015129877, dated 23.02.2023, submitted by the petitioner seeking re-issue of her passport on the following conditions:
(i) The petitioner herein shall submit an undertaking along with an affidavit in C.C.No.28 of 2023, pending on the file of learned Special Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Karimnagar District, stating that she shall not leave India during pendency of the said C.C. without permission of the Court and that she shall co- operate with trial Court in concluding the proceedings in the said C.C.
(ii) On filing such an undertaking as well as affidavit, the trial Court shall issue a certified copy of the same within two (2) weeks therefrom;
(iii) The petitioner herein shall submit an application afresh along with certified copy of this order as well as the aforesaid undertaking MSK,J wp_13045_2023 before the Passport Officer/Authority concerned for renewal of her passport.
(iv) On filing such an application, the Passport Officer/Authority shall consider the same afresh in the light of the observations made by this Court herein as well as the contents of the undertaking given by the petitioner for re-issue of her passport in accordance with law, within three (3) weeks from the date of said application.

Miscellaneous Petitions, if any, pending in this writ petition shall stand closed.
No costs.
